QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_67

question.text: What is the primary function of a Smart Order Routing (SOR) system in derivatives trading?

answer.text: To scan multiple exchanges and route orders to the exchange offering the best price
To automatically split large orders into smaller tranches over time
To verify the client's KYC and margin availability before order execution
To encrypt order data for secure transmission to the exchange

explanation.text: The Logic: A Smart Order Routing (SOR) facility is an order-routing system offered to trading members and clients which simultaneously scans the order books of multiple eligible exchanges for the same instrument and routes the order to whichever venue is currently displaying the best price (and, depending on the implementation, the best available liquidity). The objective is improved best-execution for clients in markets where the same contract is listed on more than one exchange. The Trap: Splitting a parent order into smaller child orders over time is execution-algorithm slicing (e.g., VWAP/TWAP), not SOR. Pre-trade KYC and margin checks are part of risk-management filters that sit in front of order entry. Encryption is a transport/security feature. None of these is SOR's primary function. Note: The cited workbook pages (Currency p.131-p.132 and IR p.197) list Smart Order Router as a facility/channel available to trading members and clients but do not define it explicitly as best-price routing across multiple exchanges. The framing above is general market-microstructure knowledge rather than a direct workbook citation.
